findings.title: The storage-server integration test is now skipped on Postgres instead of fixed.
findings.body: When `GRAFANA_TEST_DB=postgres`, this test now skips. That is the CI configuration where it was failing, so the startup path this PR changes (`Init` now runs inside `NewResourceServer`) is no longer tested on Postgres. The PR summary calls this "Enhanced PostgreSQL integration test compatibility", but the change turns the test off. Fix the Postgres failure, or at least link a tracking issue and make sure the test still runs in another CI job.

findings.title: Removing `Init` from every handler means `Stop` no longer blocks requests.
findings.body: `Stop` sets `s.initErr = "service is stopping"`. That only rejected requests because each handler (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob, GetBlob) called `s.Init(ctx)`, which returned `initErr`. With those calls gone, requests that arrive after `Stop` keep going to a backend that has been cancelled, and `IsHealthy` keeps reporting SERVING during shutdown. Add a cheap check for `s.initErr` (or a stopping flag) at the top of the handlers, or at least in `IsHealthy`.

findings.title: The new `TotalDocs` call reads the index cache map while the watcher may be writing to it.
findings.body: The event goroutine started just above can call `handleEvent` → `getOrCreateIndex` → `BuildIndex`, which writes `b.cache[key]`. `TotalDocs` loops over `b.cache` without holding `cacheMu`. If an event arrives right after init and creates a new index, Go can crash with "concurrent map iteration and map write". This PR also stops holding `cacheMu` around `BuildIndex`, so nothing serializes the two any more. Take `cacheMu` (or a read lock) inside `TotalDocs`, or log before starting the watcher goroutine.
